Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|1|0.source_text: No Malay explainer for Stage 1 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English (Sam, 11 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|2|0.source_text: Five sentence patterns from Kata-Kata, each with question-and-answer examples. Read the examples in pairs first, then the explanation.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Selamat pagi, Puan Aini.  B: Selamat pagi, Encik Tanaka.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Selamat tengah hari, Cik Mei Ling.  B: Selamat tengah hari, Encik Rahman.
target_spans: Selamat tengah hari, Cik Mei Ling.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Selamat petang, Pak cik.  B: Selamat petang, Encik.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Selamat malam, Mak cik.  B: Selamat malam.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Selamat datang, Encik Tanaka!  B: Terima kasih, Puan.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: Explanation: Selamat plus a time word makes a greeting: pagi (morning), tengah hari (around midday), petang (mid-afternoon to dusk), malam (night). Add a title and then the name. A title alone is also polite: Selamat pagi, Puan.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: 説明：Selamat に時間帯の語をつけるとあいさつになります。pagi（朝）、tengah hari（昼ごろ）、petang（午後〜夕方）、malam（夜）。そのあとに敬称と名前を言います。敬称だけでも丁寧です：Selamat pagi, Puan.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Titles work like さん, but they come before the name: Encik Tanaka. Selamat malam covers both こんばんは and おやすみなさい. こんにちは is split in two: Selamat tengah hari around midday, Selamat petang later.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: 日本語との比較：敬称はさんに似ていますが、名前の前に来ます。Selamat malam は「こんばんは」と「おやすみなさい」の両方です。「こんにちは」は二つに分かれます：昼ごろは Selamat tengah hari、午後は Selamat petang。

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: 1. A: Apa khabar, Encik Tanaka?  B: Khabar baik, terima kasih.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 2. A: Apa khabar, Puan Aini?  B: Baik, terima kasih.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 3. A: Apa khabar, Pak cik?  B: Baik. Terima kasih.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: 4. A: Selamat pagi, Kakak. Apa khabar?  B: Khabar baik.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|16.source_text: Explanation: Apa khabar? (literally "what news?") asks how someone is. Answer Khabar baik ("good news") or just Baik. Add the title at the end to make it personal.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|17.source_text: 説明：Apa khabar?（直訳「どんな便り？」）は相手の様子をたずねます。答えは Khabar baik（よい便り）か Baik だけでも大丈夫です。最後に敬称をつけると丁寧です。

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|18.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: It is close to お元気ですか, but Malaysians use it more widely, for example with someone they have just met.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|19.source_text: 日本語との比較：「お元気ですか」に近いですが、初めて会った人にも使えるなど、もっと広く使われます。

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|3|21.source_text: Pattern box: Khabar baik, terima kasih. (title) pula?

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 1. A: Khabar baik, terima kasih. Puan pula?  B: Saya pun baik.
target_spans: Khabar baik, terima kasih. Puan pula?

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 2. A: Baik, terima kasih. Encik pula?  B: Baik, terima kasih.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: 3. A: Khabar baik. Cik Mei Ling pula?  B: Saya pun baik, terima kasih.
target_spans: Khabar baik. Cik Mei Ling pula?

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 4. A: Saya baik. Pak cik pula?  B: Pak cik pun baik.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: Explanation: pula turns the question back to the other person ("and you?"). pun after a word means "too": Saya pun baik = I am fine too. Use the person's title, not a word for "you". Older speakers often call themselves Pak cik or Mak cik.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 説明：pula は質問を相手に返します（「あなたは？」）。pun は語のあとについて「〜も」の意味です：Saya pun baik＝私も元気です。「あなた」ではなく相手の敬称を使います。年配の人は自分を Pak cik・Mak cik と呼ぶことがよくあります。

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: pun comes after the word it adds to, just like も: Saya pun ≈ 私も. pula? ≈ 〜は？ in あなたは？

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: 日本語との比較：pun は「も」と同じく語のあとに来ます：Saya pun≈私も。pula? は「あなたは？」の「は？」に近いです。

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: 1. A: Maaf, tumpang tanya. Encik Tanaka?  B: Ya, saya Tanaka.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: 2. A: Maaf, tumpang tanya. Puan Aini?  B: Tidak. Saya Mei Ling.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: 3. A: Maaf, Pak cik. Tumpang tanya.  B: Ya?

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 4. A: Maaf, Encik Rahman?  B: Ya, saya.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: 5. A: Terima kasih, Kakak.  B: Sama-sama.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|15.source_text: Explanation: Maaf is "sorry" or "excuse me". Tumpang tanya politely asks to ask something. Confirm with ya or deny with tidak (spoken: tak). Answer thanks with Sama-sama.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|16.source_text: 説明：Maaf は「すみません・ごめんなさい」。Tumpang tanya は「ちょっとお尋ねします」。確認は ya、否定は tidak（話し言葉では tak）。お礼には Sama-sama で答えます。

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|17.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Maaf, tumpang tanya ≈ すみません、ちょっとお尋ねします. But Japanese すみません can also mean thank you; in Malay, thanks is always terima kasih.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|4|18.source_text: 日本語との比較：Maaf, tumpang tanya は「すみません、ちょっとお尋ねします」に近いです。ただし日本語の「すみません」はお礼にも使いますが、マレー語のお礼は必ず terima kasih です。

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: Pattern box: Saya minta diri dulu. Jumpa ___ !

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 1. A: Saya minta diri dulu. Jumpa esok!  B: Jumpa esok. Selamat jalan!
target_spans: Saya minta diri dulu. Jumpa esok!

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: 2. A: Maaf, saya minta diri dulu.  B: Ya. Jumpa lagi!

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: 3. A: Jumpa nanti, Cik Mei Ling.  B: Jumpa nanti.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|4.source_text: 4. A: Selamat malam, Puan. Jumpa esok.  B: Selamat malam. Jaga diri!

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: 5. A: Terima kasih, Pak cik. Jumpa lagi!  B: Hati-hati, Encik!
target_spans: Terima kasih, Pak cik. Jumpa lagi!

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: Explanation: Saya minta diri dulu means "I will take my leave first". Jumpa + esok / lagi / nanti = see you tomorrow / again / later. Selamat jalan is said to the person leaving; Selamat tinggal to the person staying, and it sounds final.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: 説明：Saya minta diri dulu は「お先に失礼します」。Jumpa ＋ esok・lagi・nanti＝また明日・またね・あとで。Selamat jalan は出かける人に、Selamat tinggal は残る人に言います。Selamat tinggal は別れの響きが強い言葉です。

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Saya minta diri dulu ≈ お先に失礼します. Careful: Selamat jalan is said by the person staying (≈ いってらっしゃい), not by the one who leaves.

Unit 1 · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: 日本語との比較：Saya minta diri dulu≈お先に失礼します。注意：Selamat jalan は残る人が言う言葉（≈いってらっしゃい）で、帰る本人は言いません。

Unit 1 · Culture and word-origin note|2|.source_text: Read where the greeting words come from and how they are used (English and Japanese).

Unit 1 · Culture and word-origin note|3|.source_text: Selamat, the first word of most greetings, comes from Arabic salāma, "wellbeing". Selamat pagi is a wish: may your morning be well. Khabar is also Arabic and means "news", so Apa khabar? asks "what news?" and Khabar baik answers "good news".
Terima kasih joins terima, "receive", and kasih, "affection": you receive someone's kindness. Tumpang tanya pairs tumpang, "ride along", with tanya, "ask": you borrow a moment of someone's time.

Two goodbyes depend on who moves. Selamat jalan, "safe going", is said to the person leaving; Selamat tinggal, "safe staying", to the person who stays. Selamat tinggal sounds final, so everyday partings use Jumpa lagi or Jumpa esok.

Titles matter. Use Encik for a man, Puan for a married or senior woman and Cik for a young woman, before the name. A title on its own is the polite "you": Puan pula? Abang and Kakak, "older brother" and "older sister", are friendly titles for waiters, drivers and shop staff of about your age; Pak cik and Mak cik, "uncle" and "auntie", are for older people.
あいさつの最初の語 Selamat は、アラビア語の salāma（無事・平安）から来ています。Selamat pagi は「よい朝でありますように」という願いです。Khabar もアラビア語で「便り」の意味なので、Apa khabar? は「どんな便り？」、Khabar baik は「よい便り」です。
Terima kasih は terima（受け取る）と kasih（愛情）から成り、相手の好意を受け取るという意味です。Tumpang tanya は tumpang（相乗りする）と tanya（たずねる）で、相手の時間を少し借りる表現です。
別れのあいさつは、だれが動くかで変わります。Selamat jalan（無事に行って）は出かける人に、Selamat tinggal（無事に残って）は残る人に言います。Selamat tinggal は別れの響きが強いので、ふだんは Jumpa lagi や Jumpa esok を使います。
敬称も大切です。男性には Encik、既婚・年上の女性には Puan、若い女性には Cik を名前の前につけます。敬称だけで丁寧な「あなた」になります：Puan pula?。Abang・Kakak（兄・姉）は同年代の店員や運転手への親しい呼びかけ、Pak cik・Mak cik（おじさん・おばさん）は年上の人への呼びかけです。

■ What to listen for · 注意点
Title before the name; no Tanaka Encik. pun after the word. Selamat jalan from the person staying.
Final k as a catch, not a full く: baik, tidak. No vowel added after final consonants: Encik, not "enchiku".
Spoken tak only after tidak has been taught, and always labelled spoken.

Unit 1 · Pronunciation and spelling bloc.source_text: マレー語のつづりと発音はほぼ規則的です。日本語話者が注意したい音を練習し、最後に書き取りをします。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 1 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English (Sam, 11 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Malay spelling is close to regular. Practise the sounds Japanese speakers find tricky, then take a short dictation.
a, i, o are close to Japanese あ, い, お. u is rounder than う: Jumpa, Puan.
e has two sounds and the spelling does not show which. Weak e (like the a in "about"): selamat, petang, terima kasih, Encik.
Clear e (like え): esok. Learn each word with its sound.
e には二つの音があり、つづりでは区別しません。弱い e（あいまい母音）：selamat、petang。はっきりした e（え）：esok。
■ 2 · Consonants · 子音
c sounds like ち: Cik, Encik, Pak cik.
ng is one sound, as in "sing" (no ぐ after it): petang, tengah hari.
kh, from Arabic, is a soft sound from the back of the throat: khabar.
Final k is a catch in the throat, not a full く: baik, tidak, Pak cik, Mak cik.
r and l are different sounds: terima kasih, diri (tap the r); selamat, lagi, malam (tongue touches for l).
No extra vowel after a final consonant: maaf, not "maafu"; malam, not "maramu". Double aa in maaf is two syllables: ma-af.
ち・ん・のどの音などに注意。語末に母音を足さないこと。r と l は別の音です。
■ 3 · Read aloud in pairs · ペアで音読
pagi · petang · malam · esok
Encik · Cik · Pak cik · Mak cik
baik · tidak · maaf
terima kasih · selamat · lagi · diri
sama-sama · hati-hati (a repeated word is written with a hyphen)
Selamat berkenalan · khabar · Apa khabar?
■ 4 · Dictation · 書き取り
Your teacher reads eight words. Write them.
Check: is there a hyphen in a repeated word? Did you write ng, c and kh correctly?
Dictation (read twice): 1 pagi 2 malam 3 esok 4 baik 5 Encik 6 khabar 7 petang 8 sama-sama.
Unverified: these pronunciation notes are from general knowledge of standard Malaysian Malay, not checked against a reference. Sam to confirm before teaching.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|2|0.source_text: Four Kata-Kata patterns with question-and-answer examples. Read the examples in pairs first, then the explanation.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: Nama saya ___ . / Ini ___ . Namanya ___ .

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Nama saya Rahman. Encik pula?  B: Nama saya Tanaka.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Ini kawan saya. Namanya Ali.  B: Selamat berkenalan, Ali.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Itu Cik Mei Ling?  B: Ya, itu Cik Mei Ling.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Nama awak Yuki?  B: Ya, nama saya Yuki.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Ini Encik Kumar. Namanya Kumar.  B: Selamat berkenalan, Encik Kumar.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: Explanation: Two nouns side by side make a sentence: Nama saya Tanaka (my name, Tanaka). There is no word for "is". saya after nama means "my". ini (this) is near you, itu (that) is further away. -nya on a noun means his, her or its: namanya = his or her name.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: 説明：名詞を二つ並べると文になります：Nama saya Tanaka。「〜です」にあたる語はありません。nama のあとの saya は「私の」。ini（これ・この）は近く、itu（それ・あれ）は遠く。名詞に -nya をつけると「彼の・彼女の・その」：namanya＝その人の名前。

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese also puts the owner first in 私の名前, but Malay puts it last: nama saya = name + me. No は, の or です are needed.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「私の名前」とは逆に、マレー語は持ち主が後ろに来ます：nama saya＝名前＋私。「は」「の」「です」はいりません。

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: 1. A: Siapa nama encik?  B: Nama saya Kimura.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 2. A: Siapa nama puan?  B: Nama saya Aini.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 3. A: Itu siapa?  B: Itu Encik Rahman.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: 4. A: Siapa nama kawan awak?  B: Namanya Mei Ling.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|16.source_text: 5. A: Dia siapa?  B: Dia kawan saya.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|17.source_text: Explanation: siapa means "who". Malay asks for a name with "who": Siapa nama encik? The question word can also stay where the answer goes: Itu siapa? (that is who?). Use the title as "you" with people you do not know well.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|18.source_text: 説明：siapa は「だれ」。名前をたずねる時も「だれ」を使います：Siapa nama encik?。疑問詞を答えの位置に置いたままでもかまいません：Itu siapa?（あれはだれ？）。よく知らない相手には「あなた」の代わりに敬称を使います。

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|19.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: お名前は何ですか uses 何 (what), but Malay uses siapa (who). Like Japanese, the question word can stay in place: Itu siapa? ≈ あれはだれ？

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 日本語との比較：「お名前は何ですか」は「何」ですが、マレー語は siapa（だれ）です。日本語と同じく、疑問詞をそのままの位置に置けます：Itu siapa?≈あれはだれ？

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: Pattern box: Saya orang ___ . Asal saya dari ___ .

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 1. A: Encik orang Jepun?  B: Ya, saya orang Jepun. Asal saya dari Osaka.
target_spans: Ya, saya orang Jepun. Asal saya dari Osaka.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: 2. A: Puan orang Malaysia?  B: Ya. Asal saya dari Ipoh.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 3. A: Kampung encik di mana?  B: Kampung saya di Sapporo.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 4. A: Mereka orang Jepun?  B: Tidak, mereka orang Malaysia.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: 5. A: Apa negara asal awak?  B: Negara asal saya Jepun.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: Explanation: orang (person) + a country = nationality: orang Jepun, orang Malaysia. asal is origin and dari is "from". A yes/no question can be a statement said with a rising voice: Encik orang Jepun?

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: 説明：orang（人）＋国名で国籍になります：orang Jepun、orang Malaysia。asal は出身、dari は「〜から」。はい・いいえの質問は、文の終わりを上げて言うだけでもできます：Encik orang Jepun?

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: orang Jepun is built like 日本人 (Japan + person), but in the opposite order: person + Japan. A rising voice works like か.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: 日本語との比較：orang Jepun は「日本人」と同じ作りですが、順番が逆です（人＋日本）。文末を上げるのは「か」と同じ働きです。

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: Pattern box: ___ di mana? / Di mana ___ ?  (unit 2B adds di manakah)

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: 1. A: Kampung encik di mana?  B: Di Osaka.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|15.source_text: 2. A: Encik Rahman di mana?  B: Dia di Kuala Lumpur.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|16.source_text: 3. A: Di mana Cik Mei Ling?  B: Dia di Bangsar.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|17.source_text: 4. A: Kampung dia di mana?  B: Kampung dia di Johor Bahru.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|18.source_text: 5. A: Osaka di mana?  B: Osaka di Jepun.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|19.source_text: Explanation: di mana is "where": di (at) + mana (which place). Put it at the end, where the answer goes, or at the front. di is written as a separate word before a place: di Osaka.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|20.source_text: 説明：di mana は「どこ」：di（〜に）＋ mana。答えが入る文末に置いても、文頭に置いてもかまいません。di は場所の前に離して書きます：di Osaka。

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|21.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Like どこ, di mana can sit where the answer goes. But di comes before the place (in Osaka), the reverse of 大阪に.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 日本語との比較：「どこ」と同じく、答えの位置に置けます。ただし di は場所の前に来ます（di Osaka）。「大阪に」とは逆です。

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: Patterns are Kata-Kata frames ms-c02-f01, f02, f03 and f08 (taught here in its plain form di mana).

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: Teacher prompts: read each A line; the class gives the B line with their own facts.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: Check: Nama saya …, not Saya nama …; orang Jepun, not Jepun orang; di Osaka with di before the place.

Unit 2A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|3.source_text: Negating a noun (bukan) is a chapter 3 word: for now learners answer Tidak, saya orang Malaysia.

Unit 2A · Culture and usage note · Choos.source_text: 「あなた」の選び方、kami と kita、名前の習慣について読みます（英語と日本語）。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 1 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English (Sam, 11 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Read how to choose "you", the difference between kami and kita, and name customs (English and Japanese).

Malay has several words for "you", and choosing one is a social decision. With someone senior or someone you have just met, avoid a pronoun and use the title: Encik pula?, Puan orang Malaysia? Awak is the everyday "you" between colleagues of a similar age. Anda is formal and impersonal: you see it on signs, forms and adverts. Kamu is for children and juniors, and engkau or kau only for very close friends; it can sound rude to a stranger. Aku, the casual "I", goes with kau.

Two words mean "we". Kami leaves the listener out; kita takes the listener in. Kami orang Jepun tells a Malaysian that you and your friends are Japanese; Jom, kita jumpa nanti includes the person you are talking to. Japanese 私たち covers both.
Dia means both "he" and "she". For a respected person, such as a manager or a minister, Malaysians often say beliau.

Names follow their own customs. In most Malay names the second part is the father's name, not a family name, so the title goes with the person's own name: Encik Rahman. Chinese Malaysian names put the family name first, as Japanese names do.

マレー語には「あなた」にあたる語がいくつもあり、どれを選ぶかは人間関係の問題です。目上の人や初対面の人には代名詞を避け、敬称を使います：Encik pula?、Puan orang Malaysia?。Awak は同年代の同僚どうしのふだんの「あなた」。Anda は改まった、相手を特定しない言い方で、看板・書類・広告で見かけます。Kamu は子どもや目下の人に、engkau・kau はごく親しい友達だけに使い、知らない人には失礼に聞こえます。くだけた「私」の Aku は kau とセットです。
「私たち」も二つあります。Kami は聞き手を含まず、kita は聞き手を含みます。Kami orang Jepun はマレーシア人に「私たちは日本人です」と伝え、Jom, kita jumpa nanti は話している相手も含みます。日本語の「私たち」は両方を表します。
Dia は「彼」と「彼女」の両方です。マネージャーや大臣など敬意を払う人には beliau がよく使われます。
名前の習慣もさまざまです。マレー系の名前の多くは、後半が父親の名前で家族の姓ではありません。そのため敬称は本人の名前につけます：Encik Rahman。中華系マレーシア人の名前は、日本人と同じく姓が先です。
Sources: Kata-Kata card notes ms-c02-006 (avoid engkau with strangers) and ms-c02-007 (dia has no gender); ledger meanings L-0037 to L-0046.
Unverified: the name-custom paragraph is general knowledge, not from Sam's notes or a cited source. Sam to confirm.

Unit 2A · Teaching plan and answer key|3.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c02 (29 cards; frames ms-c02-f01, f02). Collect Tanya Cikgu questions.
After Block B: the unit 2A cards with spaced review. Before Block E: the Dunia scene "Sembang di pantri".
After Block D: Kata-Kata cards for unit 2B (work, home, family, pe- and -an). Planning figure: about 3 hours of Kata-Kata for this unit.
Hanashishou starts at A2: no link yet. Audio: teacher-read scripts only.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say my name and nationality and ask other people theirs.
0–5 Recall (Opener): greetings at four times. Expected: Selamat pagi …, Apa khabar?, … pula?
5–10 Tanya Cikgu. 10–20 Vocabulary: point at people for pronouns; ask which "you" for a manager (expected: the title).
20–40 Patterns 1 to 4: model the A lines; the class answers with their own facts. Prompt: "Is it Saya nama or Nama saya?" Expected: Nama saya.
40–45 First substitutions: Drill 2, items 1 to 3.
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask who someone is and where they are from, and introduce a friend.
0–5 Recall: "Ask my name." Expected: Siapa nama puan? / Siapa nama encik?
5–25 Drill ladder in order, types 1 to 6. In drill 3, stress kami against kita.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped version, variant. 40–45 Pair rehearsal with real facts.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a short round of introductions and read name tags.
0–5 Recall: "Introduce your partner." Expected: Ini … Namanya … Dia orang …
5–20 Listening: the table first, the script twice (on the listening key), then the questions.
20–30 Name tags: six questions, then the learner's own tag and sentences.
30–45 Task: role cards; announce the manager's arrival at minute 38.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check my introductions in a short test and say what I can do.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill, then chapter 1 greetings with the new questions.

Unit 2A · Teaching plan and answer key|4.source_text: 15–25 Unit test. 25–35 Self-check and feedback. 35–45 Preview the Kata-Kata unit 2B cards (work, home, family).
Goal: I can join a chat in the office pantry and choose the right word for "you".
0–5 Recall: "Which "you" on a form?" Expected: anda.
5–15 Scene listening: play or read the Kata-Kata Dunia scene "Sembang di pantri" (cards ms-d-pejabat-sembang-01 to 12).
15–30 Role-play the pantry chat in threes. 30–40 Free variation: an old friend arrives (Lama tak jumpa!).
40–45 Culture note on choosing "you". No Hanashishou link at A1.
■ What to listen for · 注意点
Nama saya (not Saya nama); orang Jepun (not Jepun orang); di before the place.
A title, not awak, with seniors. kami against kita. Spoken scene words are recognised first, then used only in chat.
Not taught: dari mana (chapter 7 in the ledger) and bukan (chapter 3); use Kampung … di mana? and Tidak, … instead.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: Saya kerja di ___ . Saya (job) . / Saya belajar di ___ .

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Encik kerja di mana?  B: Saya kerja di syarikat Jepun. Saya jurutera.
target_spans: Saya kerja di syarikat Jepun. Saya jurutera.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Puan kerja di mana?  B: Saya kerja di sekolah. Saya guru.
target_spans: Saya kerja di sekolah. Saya guru.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Cik pelajar?  B: Ya, saya belajar di Universiti Malaya.
target_spans: Ya, saya belajar di Universiti Malaya.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Apa kerja dia?  B: Dia pemandu.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Encik Rahman pengurus?  B: Ya, dia pengurus pejabat kami.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: Explanation: kerja di + a place says where you work; belajar di + a place, where you study. A job is just a noun after the person: Saya jurutera. Apa kerja …? asks someone's job. kerja is everyday speech; the formal written form is bekerja (a later chapter).

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: 説明：kerja di＋場所で働いている所、belajar di＋場所で勉強している所を言います。職業は人のあとに名詞を置くだけです：Saya jurutera。Apa kerja …? で職業をたずねます。kerja は話し言葉で、書き言葉では bekerja（後の章）です。

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: di works like で in 会社で働いています. But Malay verbs never change: kerja covers 働く, 働いている and 働きます.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: 日本語との比較：di は「会社で働いています」の「で」に近いです。ただしマレー語の動詞は形が変わりません：kerja で「働く・働いている・働きます」を表します。

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|11.source_text: Pattern box: Saya tinggal di ___ ( dengan ___ ).

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: 1. A: Encik tinggal di mana?  B: Saya tinggal di Mont Kiara.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 2. A: Puan tinggal dengan siapa?  B: Saya tinggal dengan suami dan anak saya.
target_spans: Saya tinggal dengan suami dan anak saya.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 3. A: Rumah cik di mana?  B: Rumah saya di Petaling Jaya.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: 4. A: Encik ada anak?  B: Ada. Anak saya belajar di sekolah Jepun.
target_spans: Ada. Anak saya belajar di sekolah Jepun.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|16.source_text: 5. A: Keluarga awak di mana?  B: Keluarga saya di Jepun.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|17.source_text: Explanation: tinggal di = live in. dengan = with. ada = have or there is; answer a yes/no question with Ada (yes) or Tidak ada (no). The owner comes after the thing: anak saya = my child, rumah cik = your house.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|18.source_text: 説明：tinggal di＝〜に住んでいる。dengan＝〜と一緒に。ada＝ある・いる・持っている。答えは Ada（はい）か Tidak ada（いいえ）。持ち主はもののあとに来ます：anak saya＝私の子ども、rumah cik＝あなたの家。

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|19.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: dengan is close to と in 夫と住んでいます. ada covers ある, いる and 持っている.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|20.source_text: 日本語との比較：dengan は「夫と住んでいます」の「と」に近いです。ada は「ある」「いる」「持っている」をまとめて表します。

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: Pattern box: Hobi saya ___ . / Saya suka ___ .

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: 2. A: Puan suka makanan Jepun?  B: Ya, saya suka makanan Jepun.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 3. A: Anak encik suka main?  B: Ya, dia suka main dengan kawan.
target_spans: Ya, dia suka main dengan kawan.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: 4. A: Awak suka kelas ini?  B: Ya, saya suka kelas ini!

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 5. A: Isteri encik suka minuman Malaysia?  B: Tidak, dia tidak suka.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 6. A: Apa hobi cik?  B: Hobi saya karaoke dan jalan-jalan.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: Explanation: suka (like) comes before a noun or a verb: suka masakan Malaysia, suka main. tidak suka = do not like. For Hobi saya ___, pick a word from the hobby word bank (karaoke, golf, hiking, oshikatsu …) or ask your teacher.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 説明：suka（好き）は名詞や動詞の前に来ます：suka masakan Malaysia、suka main。tidak suka＝好きではない。Hobi saya ___ には趣味のことば（karaoke、golf、hiking、oshikatsu など）から選ぶか、先生に聞きましょう。

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: In Japanese the thing you like comes first (料理が好き); in Malay it comes after suka: suka masakan. No が is needed.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は「料理が好き」と好きなものが先ですが、マレー語は suka のあとです：suka masakan。「が」はいりません。

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: Pattern box: Di manakah ___ ? / Adakah ___ ? / Bolehkah ___ ?

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 1. A: Di manakah pejabat encik?  B: Pejabat saya di Kuala Lumpur.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: 2. A: Siapakah nama encik?  B: Nama saya Tanaka.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|15.source_text: 3. A: Apakah nama syarikat puan?  B: Nama syarikat saya Sakura.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|16.source_text: 4. A: Adakah encik orang Jepun?  B: Ya, saya orang Jepun.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|17.source_text: 5. A: Bolehkah saya tanya?  B: Boleh.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|18.source_text: 6. A: Adakah Cik Mei Ling pelajar?  B: Tidak, dia jurutera.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|19.source_text: Explanation: -kah on a question word makes a formal question, used in writing, forms and announcements: Siapakah, Apakah, di manakah. Adakah opens a formal yes/no question; answer Ya or Tidak. Bolehkah asks politely if something is possible; answer Boleh or Tidak boleh. In everyday speech a rising voice is enough: Encik orang Jepun?

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|20.source_text: 説明：疑問詞に -kah をつけると、書き言葉・書類・アナウンスで使う改まった質問になります：Siapakah、Apakah、di manakah。Adakah は改まった「はい・いいえ」の質問を始め、答えは Ya か Tidak。Bolehkah は「〜してもいいですか・できますか」と丁寧にたずね、答えは Boleh か Tidak boleh。ふだんの会話では文末を上げるだけで十分です：Encik orang Jepun?

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: -kah works like か, but it sits on the word being asked about, not at the end. Bolehkah saya …? ≈ 〜してもいいですか.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 日本語との比較：-kah は「か」に似ていますが、文末ではなく、たずねたい語につきます。Bolehkah saya …?≈「〜してもいいですか」。

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: Pattern box: pe- + root = a person · root + -an = a thing

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|4.source_text: 1. A: Dia pelajar?  B: Ya, dia belajar di universiti.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: 2. A: Encik pekerja syarikat ini?  B: Ya, saya pekerja syarikat ini.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: 3. A: Ada soalan?  B: Ada. Bolehkah saya tanya?

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: 4. A: Ini jawapan awak?  B: Ya, ini jawapan saya.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 5. A: Encik suka makanan Malaysia?  B: Ya, dan minuman Malaysia juga.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|9.source_text: Explanation: pe- turns a root into the person who does it: kerja → pekerja, ajar → pelajar, lawat → pelawat. With some roots the sound changes (pandu → pemandu, urus → pengurus): recognise these for now. -an turns a root into a thing: makan → makanan (food), soal → soalan (question), jawab → jawapan (b becomes p).

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|10.source_text: 説明：pe- は語根を「それをする人」にします：kerja→pekerja、ajar→pelajar、lawat→pelawat。音が変わる語（pandu→pemandu、urus→pengurus）は今は見て分かれば十分です。-an は語根を「もの」にします：makan→makanan（食べ物）、soal→soalan（質問）、jawab→jawapan（b が p に）。

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|11.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: This is like 〜者 or 〜手 (運転手) for people and 〜物 for things: makanan ≈ 食べ物, minuman ≈ 飲み物.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|12.source_text: 日本語との比較：人を表す「〜者・〜手」（運転手）、ものを表す「〜物」に似ています：makanan≈食べ物、minuman≈飲み物。

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|0.source_text: Patterns 1 to 4 are Kata-Kata frames ms-c02-f04 to f08. Box 5 is a grammar point (pe- and -an), not a frame.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|1.source_text: Teacher prompts: model the A lines; the class answers with their own facts; then pairs swap.

Unit 2B · Pattern and grammar focus|6|2.source_text: Check: kerja di / tinggal di with di; owner after the thing (anak saya); suka before what is liked; -kah on the question word.

Unit 2B · Culture and word-origin note ·.source_text: pe- と -an による語の作り方、日常語と改まった語、-kah の使われ方を読みます（英語と日本語）。
（日本語は下書きです。ネイティブ・スピーカーの確認待ち）
No Malay explainer for Stage 1 units: explainers and rubrics are in Japanese or English (Sam, 11 Nov 2026). Select 日本語 or English.
Read how pe- and -an build words, which words are everyday and which formal, and where -kah questions are used (English and Japanese).

Malay builds new words from roots, and two of the first patterns are pe- and -an. pe- names the person who does something: kerja (work) gives pekerja (worker), ajar (teach) gives pelajar (student), lawat (visit) gives pelawat (visitor), lancong (tour) gives pelancong (tourist) and tani (farming) gives petani (farmer). With some roots the sound changes: pandu gives pemandu (driver) and urus gives pengurus (manager).

-an names the thing: makan gives makanan (food), minum minuman (drink), masak masakan (cooking), baca bacaan (reading material) and tulis tulisan (writing). jawab becomes jawapan, with b turning into p.
Learn these as words first; the rule helps you guess new ones on signs. Pelawat, for example, appears on visitor badges.

Two words have an everyday and a formal partner. Cikgu is the everyday word for teacher and guru the more formal one. Kerja is natural in speech; in formal writing it becomes bekerja, which you will meet with the ber- verbs in chapter 10.
The -kah questions sound formal. You will see Siapakah, Apakah and Adakah on forms and hear them in announcements and interviews. In conversation, a rising voice is enough.

マレー語は語根から新しい語を作ります。最初に学ぶ形が pe- と -an です。pe- は「それをする人」を表します：kerja（仕事）→pekerja（従業員）、ajar（教える）→pelajar（学生）、lawat（訪ねる）→pelawat（訪問者）、lancong（旅行）→pelancong（観光客）、tani（農業）→petani（農家）。音が変わる語もあります：pandu→pemandu（運転手）、urus→pengurus（マネージャー）。
-an は「もの」を表します：makan→makanan（食べ物）、minum→minuman（飲み物）、masak→masakan（料理）、baca→bacaan（読み物）、tulis→tulisan（書いたもの）。jawab は b が p に変わって jawapan になります。
まずは単語として覚えましょう。ルールを知っていると、看板の新しい語も推測できます。たとえば Pelawat は来客用の名札に書かれています。
日常語と改まった語の組もあります。先生は日常では Cikgu、改まると guru。Kerja は会話では自然ですが、改まった書き言葉では bekerja になり、第10章の ber- 動詞で学びます。
-kah の質問は改まって聞こえます。Siapakah・Apakah・Adakah は書類で見たり、アナウンスや面接で聞いたりします。会話では文末を上げるだけで十分です。

English text: 187 words. Discussion: guess the meaning of a new -an word from its root, e.g. latihan from latih.

■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can say where I work or study, where I live and who I live with.
0–5 Recall (Opener): name, nationality, hometown, then introduce a partner.
5–10 Tanya Cikgu. 10–20 Vocabulary: say a root, learners give the pe- or -an word. Expected: tulis → tulisan.
20–40 Patterns 1 to 5. Prompt: "Where do you work?" Expected: Saya kerja di …. Ask for a hobby word each learner needs and write it on the board as a personal word.
40–45 First substitutions: Drill 2, items 1 to 4.
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask about someone's work, home, family and likes, formally and informally.
0–5 Recall: "Ask me formally where my office is." Expected: Di manakah pejabat puan?
5–25 Drill ladder, types 1 to 6. 25–40 Model conversation, gapped version, business-event variant. 40–45 Pair rehearsal.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a self-introduction about work and family and read a self-introduction message.
0–5 Recall: "Who do you live with?" Expected: Saya tinggal dengan ….
5–20 Listening: table, script twice (on the listening key), questions. 20–30 Reading: Sato's message and the reply.
30–45 Task: role cards; switch to the formal interview at minute 37.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check my self-introduction in a short test and say what I can do.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill, formal then informal; recycle chapter 1 greetings at the start of each interview.
15–25 Unit test. 25–35 Self-check and feedback. 35–45 Preview Sedia Kelas c03.

Unit 2B · Teaching plan and answer key|4.source_text: Goal: I can talk about work in an office scene and ask polite questions with bolehkah and adakah.
0–5 Recall: "Ask permission to print." Expected: Bolehkah saya cetak?
5–15 Scene listening: play or read the Kata-Kata Dunia scene "Pagi di pejabat". 15–30 Role-play it in pairs.
30–40 Free variation: the boss is on leave (cuti) and a colleague is busy (sibuk). 40–45 Culture note. No Hanashishou link at A1.
Goal: I can fill in a self-introduction form and write a short self-introduction.
0–5 Recall the four questions (work, home, family, likes). 5–15 Read the model form and paragraph.
15–30 Learners fill in the form, then write five or six sentences. 30–40 Pairs swap and check with the checklist. 40–45 Read aloud.
■ What to listen for · 注意点
di before places; the owner after the thing; suka before what is liked; -kah on the question word, not at the end.
Hobby words are the learner's own: write them on the board as personal words, not as chapter vocabulary. Raised with Sam for the ledger.
pemandu and pengurus are recognise-only. The office words from "Pagi di pejabat" are for recognition first.

Unit 3A · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Malaysian mobile numbers start with 01, for example 012, 016, 017 or 019, followed by seven or eight more digits. People read them digit by digit in small groups, usually following the dash: 012-345 6789 is kosong satu dua, tiga empat lima, enam tujuh lapan sembilan. In phone numbers most people say kosong for zero; sifar is the standard word, which you also hear in maths and formal reading. Kata-Kata card ms-c03-001 notes that kosong also means "empty" or "plain" (chapter 5). When someone reads you a number, repeat it back in the same groups to check it.
target_spans: kosong satu dua, tiga empat lima, enam tujuh lapan sembilan

Unit 3A · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Tens and teens follow a pattern that the Kata-Kata cards point out: sepuluh is se- (one) plus puluh, sebelas is se- plus belas, and dua belas is two plus belas (cards ms-c03-011 to ms-c03-013). In the same way 100, 1,000 and 1,000,000 are seratus, seribu and sejuta.

Unit 3A · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: Age matters in Malaysian conversation because it helps decide how you address people. Someone a little older is Abang or Kakak; an older man or woman is Pak cik or Mak cik (chapter 1). Asking Berapa umur …? is normal about children and on forms, for example at a bank counter. With adults you have just met, especially at work, many people do not ask directly and simply choose a polite title.

Unit 3A · Culture and usage note|3|4.source_text: マレーシアの携帯電話番号は 01 で始まり（012、016、017、019 など）、そのあとに7桁か8桁が続きます。読むときは数字を一つずつ、たいていハイフンの区切りに合わせて小さなまとまりで読みます：012-345 6789 は kosong satu dua, tiga empat lima, enam tujuh lapan sembilan。電話番号のゼロはたいてい kosong と言います。sifar は標準語で、算数や改まった読み上げでも聞きます。Kata-Kata カード ms-c03-001 によると、kosong には「空の」「何も入っていない」という意味もあります（第5章）。番号を読み上げてもらったら、同じ区切りで繰り返して確認しましょう。
target_spans: kosong satu dua, tiga empat lima, enam tujuh lapan sembilan

Unit 3A · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 10や11〜19の数には、Kata-Kata カードが示すきまりがあります：sepuluh は se-（1）＋puluh、sebelas は se-＋belas、dua belas は2＋belas です（カード ms-c03-011〜013）。同じように100・1000・100万は seratus・seribu・sejuta です。

Unit 3A · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: マレーシアの会話では、相手をどう呼ぶかを決めるのに年齢が関わります。少し年上の人は Abang・Kakak、年配の男性・女性は Pak cik・Mak cik です（第1章）。子どもについてや書類では Berapa umur …? と聞くのは普通で、銀行の窓口でもそうです。ただし、初対面の大人、特に仕事の場では、直接年齢を聞かずに丁寧な呼び方を選ぶ人も多くいます。

Unit 3B · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Malaysian prices are in ringgit (RM) and sen, and RM1 is 100 sen. Say the ringgit first, then the sen: RM8.50 is lapan ringgit lima puluh sen. Kata-Kata card ms-c03-021 gives RM12.50 as dua belas ringgit lima puluh sen. In quick speech people often drop the word sen, but in class say the full amount.
target_spans: dua belas ringgit lima puluh sen

Unit 3B · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Cash totals are rounded. Since 2008, Bank Negara Malaysia’s rounding mechanism has rounded the total of a bill paid over the counter to the nearest 5 sen: totals ending in 1, 2, 6 or 7 sen go down, and totals ending in 3, 4, 8 or 9 sen go up. It applies to the total bill, not to each item, and card or QR payments are charged the exact amount. So a total of RM8.52 paid in cash becomes RM8.50.

Unit 3B · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: Small stalls and pasar sellers often prefer cash, but many also display a DuitNow QR code, Malaysia’s national QR payment standard, which you can scan with a banking or e-wallet app. At markets and small stalls, polite bargaining is common: Kurang sikit, boleh? (spoken). It is not done in supermarkets or shops with fixed prices. Both wang (standard) and duit (everyday) mean money (card ms-c03-022).

Unit 3B · Culture and usage note|3|4.source_text: マレーシアの値段はリンギット（RM）とセンで、RM1は100センです。リンギット、センの順に言います：RM8.50 は lapan ringgit lima puluh sen。Kata-Kata カード ms-c03-021 では RM12.50 を dua belas ringgit lima puluh sen としています。早口では sen を省くこともよくありますが、授業では全部言いましょう。
target_spans: dua belas ringgit lima puluh sen

Unit 3B · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 現金の合計は端数が丸められます。2008年からマレーシア中央銀行（Bank Negara Malaysia）の端数処理の仕組みにより、窓口で支払う請求額の合計は5セン単位に丸められます：末尾が1・2・6・7センなら切り下げ、3・4・8・9センなら切り上げです。対象は品物ごとではなく合計額で、カードやQRでの支払いは端数まで正確に請求されます。たとえば合計 RM8.52 を現金で払うと RM8.50 になります。

Unit 3B · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 屋台や pasar の売り手は現金を好むことが多いですが、マレーシアの全国共通QR決済規格 DuitNow QR のコードを置いている店も多く、銀行アプリや電子ウォレットで読み取って払えます。市場や小さな屋台では、丁寧に値切るのは普通です：Kurang sikit, boleh?（話し言葉）。スーパーや定価の店では値切りません。wang（標準語）と duit（日常語）はどちらも「お金」です（カード ms-c03-022）。

Unit 3B · Teaching plan and answer key|3.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c03; read the numerical cards relevant to this unit.
Before Block E: Kata-Kata Dunia "Pasar pagi"; recognise its scene vocabulary.
After Block D: Kata-Kata chapter 3 cards, frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours per full-course unit.
No Hanashishou A1 scene. Listening uses the printed teacher script, not an audio file.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can ask a price and say an amount in ringgit and sen.
0–5 Recall: chapters 1 and 2 (greeting, name, origin). 5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions.
10–20 core vocabulary, with recognition and revision categories kept separate.
20–40 the four or five pattern boxes, Q&A first, rule second. 40–45 first substitutions.
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can pay with cash or card and confirm the change.
0–5 Recall first pattern without notes. 5–25 six drills in section 14 order.
25–40 model conversation then gaps then changed-facts variant. 40–45 pair rehearsal.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can understand a short market transaction and read a price list.
0–5 Recall two number sentences. 5–20 teacher-read listening, two readings.
20–30 six reading questions and writing. 30–45 role-play; change the plan mid-way.
■ Block D · Review and test (45 min)
Goal: I can check transaction language and arithmetic in a low-stakes test.
0–15 mixed recall with cumulative question words including berapa, adakah and bolehkah.
15–25 low-stakes unit test; 25–35 self-check and correction; 35–45 Kata-Kata preview.
■ Block E · Dunia scene (45 min)
Goal: I can recognise words in a morning-market scene.
0–5 recall. 5–15 teacher-read Dunia scene. 15–30 pairs enact the scene.
30–40 change the situation and speak freely; 40–45 usage/culture discussion.
■ What to listen for · 注意点
Use explicit fictional price labels and never substitute current local prices.
Standard wang precedes everyday duit; sahaja precedes spoken saja.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: Ini kali [pertama / kedua / ketiga] saya di ___.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Ini kali pertama encik di Malaysia? B: Ya, kali pertama.
target_spans: Ini kali pertama encik di Malaysia?

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Ini kali kedua encik di pasar ini? B: Ya, kali kedua.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Ini kali ketiga encik di pejabat pos ini? B: Bukan, kali kedua.
target_spans: Ini kali ketiga encik di pejabat pos ini?

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Ini kali kesepuluh encik di Malaysia? B: Ya, kali kesepuluh!
target_spans: Ini kali kesepuluh encik di Malaysia?

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: Explanation: kali counts occasions. First is pertama (irregular); from two onwards the ordinal is built on the number: dua → kedua, tiga → ketiga, sepuluh → kesepuluh.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: 説明：kali は回数です。「1回目」は不規則な pertama。2以降は数字から作ります：dua→kedua、tiga→ketiga、sepuluh→kesepuluh。

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 〜回目 attaches to every number, including 1回目. Malay first is a separate word, pertama.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「〜回目」は1にも付きますが、マレー語の「1回目」は別の語 pertama です。

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|11.source_text: 1. A: Diskaun berapa peratus? B: Sepuluh peratus.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: 2. A: Diskaun dua puluh peratus? B: Ya, dua puluh peratus.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 3. A: Diskaun lima puluh peratus? B: Bukan, sepuluh peratus.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 4. A: Harga sebelum diskaun sepuluh ringgit. Selepas diskaun? B: Lapan ringgit.
target_spans: Harga sebelum diskaun sepuluh ringgit. Selepas diskaun?

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: Explanation: peratus follows the number: dua puluh peratus (20%). Use sebelum and selepas for the price before and after the discount.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|16.source_text: 説明：peratus は数字の後ろです：dua puluh peratus（20%）。割引前・割引後の値段は sebelum・selepas で言います。

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|17.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese signs often say 2割引 as well as 20%OFF. Malay signs use the percentage.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|18.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本では「2割引」とも書きますが、マレー語の表示はパーセントです。

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|21.source_text: 1. A: Berapa panjang bungkusan ini? B: Tiga puluh sentimeter.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|22.source_text: 2. A: Berapa lebar bungkusan ini? B: Dua puluh sentimeter.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|23.source_text: 3. A: Berapa tinggi bungkusan ini? B: Sepuluh sentimeter.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|3|24.source_text: 4. A: Berapa berat bungkusan ini? B: Dua kilo.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: Explanation: In speech, ask with berapa plus the adjective, and answer with the number and unit (Panjang tiga puluh sentimeter). The nouns ketinggian, kepanjangan, kelebaran and kedalaman are the written forms you see on forms and labels.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 説明：会話では berapa ＋形容詞でたずね、数字と単位で答えます（Panjang tiga puluh sentimeter）。ketinggian・kepanjangan・kelebaran・kedalaman は書類やラベルで見る書き言葉の名詞です。

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese 長さ・幅・高さ are everyday words, but kepanjangan and kelebaran are formal. For 長さは？ in conversation say Berapa panjang?

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「長さ・幅・高さ」は会話でも使いますが、kepanjangan・kelebaran は改まった語です。会話の「長さは？」は Berapa panjang? です。

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: Pattern box: Fractions and decimals: setengah, suku, perpuluhan.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 1. A: Berapa kilo? B: Setengah kilo.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: 2. A: Berapa kilo? B: Suku kilo.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 3. A: Berapa kilo? B: Tiga suku kilo.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: 4. A: Berat satu perpuluhan lima kilo? B: Ya, satu perpuluhan lima kilo.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: Explanation: setengah (or separuh) is a half, suku a quarter, tiga suku three quarters. perpuluhan reads the decimal point: 1.5 = satu perpuluhan lima.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: 説明：setengah（または separuh）＝半分、suku＝4分の1、tiga suku＝4分の3。perpuluhan は小数点の読み方です：1.5＝satu perpuluhan lima。

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese reads 1.5 as いってんご. Malay reads the point as a word, perpuluhan.

Unit 3C · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語の「いってんご」の「てん」に当たるのが perpuluhan です。

Unit 3C · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Malaysia uses the metric system. At a pasar (a wet market or morning market), fruit, vegetables and fish are sold by weight, and the seller weighs your order on a scale. Asking for setengah kilo or suku kilo is normal; you do not have to buy a whole kilo. Shop signs show discounts as percentages, such as Diskaun 20%, read aloud as diskaun dua puluh peratus. Decimals are read with perpuluhan: 1.5 kilo is satu perpuluhan lima kilo (Kata-Kata card ms-c03-044).

Unit 3C · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: For sizes, everyday speech uses the adjective itself: Berapa panjang bungkusan ini? Panjang tiga puluh sentimeter. The nouns ketinggian, kepanjangan, kelebaran and kedalaman are built from tinggi, panjang, lebar and dalam (Kata-Kata cards ms-c03-050 to ms-c03-053). You meet them mostly in writing: on forms, labels and product descriptions. kepanjangan can also mean the full form of an abbreviation, so in conversation panjang is the safer choice.

Unit 3C · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: For ordinals, pertama is irregular: everyday Malay does not say kesatu (Kata-Kata card ms-c03-036). From two onwards the ordinal is built on the number: dua → kedua, tiga → ketiga. Ini kali pertama saya di Malaysia is a natural thing to say when you meet someone new, and a Malaysian may well ask Ini kali pertama encik di Malaysia? when you arrive.
target_spans: Ini kali pertama saya di Malaysia
Ini kali pertama encik di Malaysia?

Unit 3C · Culture and usage note|3|4.source_text: マレーシアはメートル法を使います。pasar（ウェットマーケットや朝市）では果物・野菜・魚を重さで売り、店の人がはかりで量ってくれます。setengah kilo（500グラム）や suku kilo（250グラム）を頼むのは普通で、1キロ単位で買う必要はありません。店の割引表示は Diskaun 20% のようにパーセントで書かれ、diskaun dua puluh peratus と読みます。小数は perpuluhan で読みます：1.5キロは satu perpuluhan lima kilo（Kata-Kata カード ms-c03-044）。

Unit 3C · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 大きさを言うとき、日常の会話では形容詞をそのまま使います：Berapa panjang bungkusan ini?（この小包の長さは？）Panjang tiga puluh sentimeter.（長さ30センチです）。ketinggian・kepanjangan・kelebaran・kedalaman は tinggi・panjang・lebar・dalam から作られた名詞です（Kata-Kata カード ms-c03-050〜053）。主に書類・ラベル・商品説明などの書き言葉で見かけます。kepanjangan は略語の「正式名称」の意味でも使われるので、会話では panjang を使うほうが無難です。

Unit 3C · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 序数では pertama（1番目）が不規則で、日常では kesatu とは言いません（Kata-Kata カード ms-c03-036）。2以降は数字から作ります：dua→kedua、tiga→ketiga。Ini kali pertama saya di Malaysia（マレーシアは初めてです）は初対面でよく使う自然な一言で、到着したときに Ini kali pertama encik di Malaysia?（マレーシアは初めてですか）と聞かれることもよくあります。
target_spans: Ini kali pertama saya di Malaysia
Ini kali pertama encik di Malaysia?

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: Pukul berapa sekarang? / Sekarang pukul ___ (pagi / tengah hari / petang / malam).

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Pukul berapa sekarang? B: Sekarang pukul sembilan pagi.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Pukul berapa sekarang? B: Sekarang pukul empat suku petang.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Pukul berapa sekarang? B: Pukul dua setengah.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Sekarang pukul berapa, puan? B: Pukul sebelas empat puluh lima minit.
target_spans: Pukul sebelas empat puluh lima minit.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: 5. A: Pukul berapa sekarang? B: Pukul satu tengah hari.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: Explanation: pukul comes before the hour. Then add the minutes: suku for :15, setengah for :30, or the number of minutes (empat puluh lima minit for :45). Add pagi, tengah hari, petang or malam when the part of the day is not obvious.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: 説明：pukul は時の数字の前に置きます。分は suku（15分）、setengah（30分）、または分の数（45分なら empat puluh lima minit）で言います。時間帯がはっきりしないときは pagi・tengah hari・petang・malam を付けます。

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Like 〜時, pukul marks clock time, but it comes before the number. The part of the day works like 午前・午後, but it goes at the end: pukul empat petang = 午後4時.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|9.source_text: 日本語との比較：「〜時」と同じく時刻を表しますが、pukul は数字の前に来ます。時間帯は午前・午後に似ていますが、最後に置きます：pukul empat petang＝午後4時。

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|11.source_text: Pattern box: Hari ini hari apa? / Hari ini hari bulan berapa? / Apa tarikh hari ini?

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: 1. A: Hari ini hari apa? B: Hari ini hari Khamis.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 2. A: Semalam hari apa? B: Semalam hari Rabu.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 3. A: Lusa hari apa? B: Lusa hari Sabtu.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: 4. A: Hari ini hari bulan berapa? B: Hari bulan sebelas.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|16.source_text: 5. A: Apa tarikh hari ini? B: Sebelas November.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|17.source_text: 6. A: Apa tarikh kelas pertama? B: Lima Januari.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|3|18.source_text: Explanation: Put hari before the name of the day: hari Isnin. Hari apa? asks the day of the week. Hari ini hari bulan berapa? asks the day of the month: answer hari bulan + the number, hari bulan sebelas (the 11th). Apa tarikh hari ini? asks the full date: the day, then the month, sebelas November. Days around today: kelmarin, semalam, hari ini, esok, lusa.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 説明：曜日の名前の前に hari を置きます：hari Isnin。Hari apa? は曜日をたずねます。Hari ini hari bulan berapa? は「何日」をたずね、hari bulan＋数で答えます：hari bulan sebelas（11日）。Apa tarikh hari ini? は日付全体をたずね、日、月の順で答えます：sebelas November（11月11日）。今日の前後：kelmarin（おととい）、semalam（昨日）、hari ini（今日）、esok（明日）、lusa（あさって）。

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Malay has one word each for おととい (kelmarin) and あさって (lusa), as Japanese does and English does not. The day names are not built from 月・火・水, so learn them as words. Dates go day first, then month (sebelas November), the reverse of 11月11日; most month names are close to English (Januari, Ogos = August).

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: 日本語との比較：おととい（kelmarin）とあさって（lusa）にそれぞれ一語あるのは日本語と同じで、英語とは違います。曜日の名前は月・火・水のような組み立てではないので、単語として覚えます。日付は日、月の順（sebelas November）で、11月11日とは逆です。月の名前の多くは英語に近い語です（Januari、Ogos＝8月）。

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: Pattern box: Saya ___ setiap ___ . / Saya [selalu / biasanya / kadang-kadang / jarang / tidak pernah] ___ .

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 1. A: Encik main badminton? B: Ya, setiap hari Sabtu.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: 2. A: Puan selalu masak? B: Kadang-kadang sahaja.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: 3. A: Encik selalu kerja di rumah? B: Jarang. Biasanya saya kerja di pejabat.
target_spans: Jarang. Biasanya saya kerja di pejabat.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|8.source_text: 4. A: Cik Farah belajar bahasa Jepun? B: Ya, seminggu sekali, hari Rabu.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: 5. A: Awak main golf? B: Tidak pernah.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: Explanation: A frequency word goes before the verb (Saya selalu masak) or, for biasanya and kadang-kadang, often at the start. setiap + time comes after the activity: setiap hari, setiap hari Sabtu. For a count use sekali or a number + kali: seminggu sekali, dua kali seminggu.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: 説明：頻度の語は動詞の前（Saya selalu masak）、biasanya・kadang-kadang は文頭にもよく来ます。setiap＋時は活動のあと：setiap hari、setiap hari Sabtu。回数は sekali か 数＋kali：seminggu sekali（週に一回）、dua kali seminggu（週に二回）。

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: 毎日・いつも・時々 map closely to setiap hari, selalu, kadang-kadang. Watch tidak pernah: it means "never" as a habit, not 〜しない once.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 日本語との比較：毎日・いつも・時々 は setiap hari・selalu・kadang-kadang にほぼ対応します。tidak pernah は習慣として「一度も〜ない」で、一回だけ「しない」という意味ではありません。

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|4|15.source_text: Pattern box: Bila ___ ? / Berapa jam? (pukul = clock time, jam = how long)

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 1. A: Bila kelas encik? B: Hari Selasa, pukul tujuh setengah malam.
target_spans: Hari Selasa, pukul tujuh setengah malam.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: 2. A: Kelas berapa jam? B: Dua jam.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: 3. A: Bila kita main badminton? B: Hari Sabtu ini, pukul lapan pagi.
target_spans: Hari Sabtu ini, pukul lapan pagi.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: 4. A: Encik main berapa jam? B: Biasanya satu jam setengah.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|4.source_text: 5. A: Bila encik cuti? B: Dua minggu lagi.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|5.source_text: Explanation: bila asks "when?" and is answered with a day, a date or a time. Pukul berapa? asks only for the clock time. pukul tiga is three o'clock; tiga jam is three hours. In casual speech many people also say jam tiga for three o'clock: that is fine too, but this course practises pukul tiga.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|6.source_text: 説明：bila は「いつ」で、曜日・日付・時刻で答えます。Pukul berapa? は時刻だけをたずねます。pukul tiga は3時、tiga jam は3時間です。くだけた会話では3時を jam tiga と言う人も多く、それも正しいですが、このコースでは pukul tiga を練習します。

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|7.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: いつ = bila. Japanese separates 時 and 時間 with a suffix; Malay uses two different words in two positions: pukul tiga (before) and tiga jam (after).

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|5|8.source_text: 日本語との比較：いつ＝bila。日本語は「時」と「時間」を語尾で区別しますが、マレー語は別の語を別の位置に置きます：pukul tiga（前）と tiga jam（後）。

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|3.source_text: Pattern 2: hari apa asks the weekday; hari bulan berapa asks the day of the month (hari bulan + number); tarikh is the full date, day before month.

Unit 4A · Pattern and grammar focus|6|4.source_text: Pattern 4: if a learner answers Bila? with only a clock time, accept it; then ask Hari apa?

Unit 4A · Culture and usage note|2|0.source_text: Read about how time and routines are talked about in Malaysia. Word-building notes come only from Kata-Kata card notes.

Unit 4A · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: In everyday speech most Malaysians use the 12-hour clock and add the part of the day: pukul tujuh pagi (7 a.m.), pukul satu tengah hari (1 p.m.), pukul empat petang (4 p.m.) and pukul sembilan malam (9 p.m.). Petang covers the afternoon until about sunset; after dark it is malam. Quarters and halves come from chapter 3: pukul empat suku is 4:15 and pukul dua setengah is 2:30. For 4:45, say the minutes: pukul empat empat puluh lima minit. In casual talk you may also hear jam used for the clock time; in this course pukul is for the clock and jam for how long.
target_spans: pukul empat empat puluh lima minit

Unit 4A · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Two card notes in Kata-Kata show how frequency words are built: seminggu sekali (once a week) is se- (one) + minggu, then sekali (card ms-c04-034), and biasanya is biasa (usual) + -nya (card ms-c04-030).

Unit 4A · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: All of Malaysia keeps one time, Malaysian Standard Time (UTC+8). Until the end of 1981 Peninsular Malaysia was half an hour behind Sabah and Sarawak; on 1 January 1982 it moved its clocks forward 30 minutes so the whole country shares one time. Malaysia is one hour behind Japan, so 9 a.m. in Tokyo is 8 a.m. in Kuala Lumpur.

Unit 4A · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: In Kuala Lumpur and Selangor most offices work Monday to Friday, and the weekend (hujung minggu) is Saturday and Sunday. Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu have a Friday and Saturday weekend instead; Johor moved back to Saturday and Sunday on 1 January 2025. In Peninsular Malaysia the Employment Act 1955 limits normal working hours to 45 a week; the limit came down from 48 hours on 1 January 2023.

Unit 4A · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: 日常会話では、ほとんどのマレーシア人は12時間制で時刻を言い、時間帯を付け加えます：pukul tujuh pagi（午前7時）、pukul satu tengah hari（午後1時）、pukul empat petang（午後4時）、pukul sembilan malam（午後9時）。petang は午後から日没ごろまでで、暗くなると malam です。15分と30分は第3章の語を使います：pukul empat suku は4時15分、pukul dua setengah は2時30分です。4時45分は分の数で言います：pukul empat empat puluh lima minit。くだけた会話では時刻に jam を使う人もいますが、このコースでは時刻は pukul、かかる時間は jam で言います。
target_spans: pukul empat empat puluh lima minit

Unit 4A · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: Kata-Kata のカード注記に、頻度の語の成り立ちが二つあります：seminggu sekali（週に一回）は se-（一つ）＋minggu、そのあとに sekali（カード ms-c04-034）。biasanya は biasa（ふつうの）＋-nya（カード ms-c04-030）です。

Unit 4A · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: マレーシア全土は一つの時刻、マレーシア標準時（UTC+8）を使っています。1981年末まで、マレー半島はサバ州・サラワク州より30分遅れていましたが、1982年1月1日に時計を30分進め、国全体が同じ時刻になりました。マレーシアは日本より1時間遅いので、東京の午前9時はクアラルンプールの午前8時です。

Unit 4A · Culture and usage note|4|0.source_text: クアラルンプールとセランゴール州では、ほとんどの職場が月曜日から金曜日まで働き、週末（hujung minggu）は土曜日と日曜日です。ケダ州、クランタン州、トレンガヌ州では金曜日と土曜日が週末です。ジョホール州は2025年1月1日に土曜日・日曜日の週末に戻りました。マレー半島では、1955年雇用法により通常の労働時間は週45時間までと決められています。この上限は2023年1月1日に48時間から引き下げられました。

Unit 4A · Culture and usage note|5|1.source_text: Sources: Kata-Kata cards ms-c04-030 and ms-c04-034 (word-building); Malaysian Standard Time Act 1981 and the 1982 change (see docs/STEP-5b-report.md for the references checked); the Saturday and Sunday weekend in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur (The Star, 9 Dec 2013); Friday and Saturday in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu and Johor's return to Saturday and Sunday on 1 Jan 2025 (Bernama and The Star, 7 Oct 2024; Malay Mail, 18 Jan 2025); Employment Act 1955 as amended by the Employment (Amendment) Act 2022, in force 1 January 2023 (Department of Labour Peninsular Malaysia).

Unit 4A · Teaching plan and answer key|3.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c04 (26 cards, frames ms-c04-f01 and ms-c04-f02).
Before Block E: Kata-Kata Dunia "Hujan petang" and "Cuti ke pantai"; learners only need to recognise the scene words.
After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 4 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c04-f01, ms-c04-f02 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).
Hanashishou starts at A2, so there is no Hanashishou scene for this unit. Listening uses the teacher-read script.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can tell the time, name the days and say how often I do something.
0–5 Recall: chapter 3 prices, ages and phone numbers (opener prompts).
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first; Dunia and revision words are only pointed out.
20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 to 4 (clock time, days and dates, frequency, bila and jam), Q&A first, rule second.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask and answer when something happens with bila, hari apa and pukul berapa.
0–5 Recall: say the time now and the day today without notes.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, transformation, question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can understand a class timetable and arrange a weekly activity.
0–5 Recall: learners ask each other Bila …? about their week.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.

Unit 4A · Teaching plan and answer key|4.source_text: Goal: I can check my time, day and frequency language in a short test.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 4, including bila, pukul berapa, hari apa), then chapter 3 numbers.
35–45 Preview: unit 4B cards in Kata-Kata (sudah, belum, sedang, akan; daily verbs).
Goal: I can recognise weather and holiday words in two Kata-Kata Dunia scenes.
0–5 Recall: the weather today and the time now.
5–15 Kata-Kata Dunia scenes "Hujan petang" and "Cuti ke pantai" as listening (teacher reads, learners point to pictures or words).
30–40 Free variation: the weather changes (it starts to rain), or a holiday flight moves to another day.
■ What to listen for · 注意点
pukul before the number for clock time; jam after the number for how long.
Do not teach kurang suku. For :45 say the minutes: pukul empat empat puluh lima minit (Sam, ledger Journal).
target_spans: pukul empat empat puluh lima minit

Unit 4A · Teaching plan and answer key|4.source_text: Dates (Sam, 12 Nov 2026): Hari ini hari apa? asks the weekday; Hari ini hari bulan berapa? asks the day of the month (Hari bulan sebelas., hari bulan first); Apa tarikh hari ini? asks the full date (Sebelas November.). Sam notes that Hari ini hari bulan apa? is also heard and can be taken as the weekday or the date depending on the listener; teach the two clear questions and accept either answer to it.
Use only root verbs from chapters 2 to 4 (main, kerja, belajar, masak). Daily-routine verbs come in unit 4B.
Dunia words from "Hujan petang" and "Cuti ke pantai" are for recognition in Block E only.

Unit 4A · Teaching plan and answer key|5.source_text: Answer keys are on each component. Japanese text awaits native review.
Standard forms first; spoken forms are labelled. No productive ber- or me- verbs (root verbs only).

You will learn ke in chapter 7; for now pergi kerja and balik rumah are what people say.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|0.source_text: Pattern box: Sudah ___ ? / Sudah. / Belum. (spoken: Dah ___ ?)

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|1.source_text: 1. A: Sudah makan? B: Sudah, terima kasih.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|2.source_text: 2. A: Encik sudah sampai? B: Belum. Lima minit lagi.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|3.source_text: 3. A: Bos sudah datang? B: Belum. Dia akan datang pukul sepuluh.
target_spans: Belum. Dia akan datang pukul sepuluh.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|4.source_text: 4. A: Mesyuarat sudah habis? B: Sudah. Habis pukul empat.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|5.source_text: Explanation: sudah before the verb means it has happened. belum means not yet: it is still expected. A short answer is just the marker: Sudah. / Belum. The verb itself never changes.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|6.source_text: 説明：sudah を動詞の前に置くと「もう〜した」。belum は「まだ〜していない」で、これから起こることを表します。短く答えるときは Sudah.／Belum. だけで十分です。動詞の形は変わりません。

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|7.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: sudah ≈ もう, belum ≈ まだ〜ていない. Japanese changes the verb (食べた / 食べていない); Malay keeps makan and changes only the marker.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|8.source_text: 日本語との比較：sudah ≈ もう、belum ≈ まだ〜ていない。日本語は動詞の形が変わります（食べた／食べていない）が、マレー語は makan のままで、前の語だけが変わります。

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|10.source_text: Pattern box: Saya sedang ___ . / Saya masih ___ . (spoken: tengah)

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|11.source_text: 1. A: Encik Tanaka di mana? B: Dia sedang makan.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|12.source_text: 2. A: Puan sibuk? B: Ya, saya masih ada kerja.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|13.source_text: 3. A: Anak encik sudah bangun? B: Belum, dia masih tidur.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|14.source_text: 4. A: Awak di mana sekarang? B: Saya tengah makan. (spoken)

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|15.source_text: Explanation: sedang means in the middle of doing something now. masih means still: it started before and has not stopped. In speech tengah replaces sedang.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|16.source_text: 説明：sedang は「今〜しているところ」。masih は「まだ〜している」で、前に始まってまだ終わっていないことを表します。話し言葉では sedang の代わりに tengah を使います。

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|17.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Both translate as 〜ている, but 〜ている also means a finished state (結婚している). sedang is only for an action in progress.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|3|18.source_text: 日本語との比較：どちらも「〜ている」と訳せますが、日本語の「〜ている」は結果の状態（結婚している）も表します。sedang は進行中の動作だけです。

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|0.source_text: 1. A: Bila encik akan balik? B: Saya akan balik pukul tujuh.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|1.source_text: 2. A: Minggu depan encik cuti? B: Ya, saya akan cuti seminggu.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|2.source_text: 3. A: Bos akan datang hari ini? B: Tidak. Dia akan datang esok.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|3.source_text: 4. A: Bila kelas akan mula? B: Kelas akan mula lusa.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|4.source_text: Explanation: akan before the verb means will. When a future time word is already there (esok, minggu depan), many speakers leave akan out: Esok saya cuti.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|5.source_text: 説明：akan を動詞の前に置くと「〜する予定・〜するつもり」。esok・minggu depan など未来の時の語があれば、akan を省くこともよくあります：Esok saya cuti.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|6.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: Japanese uses the same form for now and later (明日行きます). Malay can do the same with a time word; akan adds 〜する予定.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|7.source_text: 日本語との比較：日本語は現在と未来で同じ形を使います（明日行きます）。マレー語も時の語があれば同じですが、akan を付けると「〜する予定」がはっきりします。

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|9.source_text: Pattern box: Saya pernah ___ . / Saya belum pernah ___ . / Saya tidak pernah ___ .

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|10.source_text: 1. A: Encik pernah main golf? B: Pernah, dua kali.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|11.source_text: 2. A: Puan pernah tinggal di Jepun? B: Belum pernah.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|12.source_text: 3. A: Encik pernah makan masakan Melayu? B: Pernah. Saya selalu makan masakan Melayu.
target_spans: Pernah. Saya selalu makan masakan Melayu.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|13.source_text: 4. A: Encik pernah cuti di Malaysia? B: Pernah. Tahun lepas, di Penang.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|14.source_text: Explanation: pernah means have done at least once (experience). belum pernah is not yet, but it may happen; tidak pernah is never (unit 4A).

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|15.source_text: 説明：pernah は「〜したことがある」（経験）。belum pernah は「まだ〜したことがない」（これからあり得る）、tidak pernah は「一度も〜ない」（ユニット4A）です。

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|16.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: pernah ≈ 〜たことがある, and belum pernah ≈ まだ〜たことがない. The verb stays the same.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|17.source_text: 日本語との比較：pernah ≈ 〜たことがある、belum pernah ≈ まだ〜たことがない。動詞の形は変わりません。

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|19.source_text: Pattern box: ___ mula pukul ___ dan habis pukul ___ .

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|20.source_text: 1. A: Mesyuarat mula pukul berapa? B: Mesyuarat mula pukul tiga dan habis pukul lima.
target_spans: Mesyuarat mula pukul tiga dan habis pukul lima.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|21.source_text: 2. A: Kelas habis pukul berapa? B: Habis pukul sembilan setengah malam.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|4|22.source_text: 3. A: Waktu pejabat pukul berapa? B: Pukul sembilan pagi sampai pukul enam petang.
target_spans: Pukul sembilan pagi sampai pukul enam petang.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|0.source_text: 4. A: Encik sampai pukul berapa? B: Saya sampai awal, pukul lapan suku.
target_spans: Saya sampai awal, pukul lapan suku.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|1.source_text: Explanation: mula means to start and habis to finish (and also to run out). sampai means to arrive, and also until: sampai pukul enam. awal is early and lambat is late.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|2.source_text: 説明：mula は「始まる」、habis は「終わる」（「なくなる」の意味も）。sampai は「着く」と「〜まで」：sampai pukul enam。awal は早い、lambat は遅い。

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|3.source_text: Japanese helps or misleads: One word mula covers both 始まる and 始める. sampai is both 着く and 〜まで, so read the sentence for the meaning.

Unit 4B · Pattern and grammar focus|5|4.source_text: 日本語との比較：mula 一語で「始まる」も「始める」も表します。sampai は「着く」と「〜まで」の両方なので、文の中で意味を判断します。

Unit 4B · Culture and usage note|3|0.source_text: Among Malaysians, Sudah makan? (Have you eaten?) is a friendly way to check in with someone, at work as well as at home, and it often turns into an invitation: Belum? Jom makan! The Kata-Kata chapter 4 scene Sudah makan? shows exactly this exchange between two colleagues at lunchtime.

Unit 4B · Culture and usage note|3|1.source_text: Answer with Belum (not yet), not Tidak, for anything that is expected to happen: eating, arriving, finishing work, sending a file. Belum keeps the door open; Tidak says "no" and can sound like a refusal.

Unit 4B · Culture and usage note|3|2.source_text: In conversation and in text messages you will hear the spoken forms dah for sudah and tengah for sedang: Dah makan? Tengah makan. Learn the standard forms first, and recognise the spoken ones when you hear them. Both balik and pulang mean going back home; balik is the one you hear most in everyday talk.

Unit 4B · Culture and usage note|3|3.source_text: The Kata-Kata cards add some word notes. minggu depan is next week and minggu lepas is last week (cards ms-c04-019 and ms-c04-020); depan also means "front", and lepas also means "after". The card for baru (ms-c04-041) notes that the same word means "new", which you will meet in chapter 6.

Unit 4B · Culture and usage note|3|5.source_text: マレーシアでは、Sudah makan?（もう食べた？）は相手の様子を気づかう親しいあいさつで、職場でも家庭でも使われます。そこから誘いになることもよくあります：Belum? Jom makan!（まだ？じゃあ食べに行こう！）。Kata-Kata 第4章の場面 Sudah makan? は、昼休みの同僚二人のまさにこのやりとりです。

Unit 4B · Culture and usage note|3|6.source_text: 食事・到着・仕事の終わり・ファイルの送信など、これから起こるはずのことには Tidak ではなく Belum（まだ）で答えます。Belum はこれからの可能性を残しますが、Tidak は「いいえ」で、断っているように聞こえることがあります。

Unit 4B · Culture and usage note|3|7.source_text: 会話やメッセージでは、sudah の代わりに dah、sedang の代わりに tengah という話し言葉をよく聞きます：Dah makan? Tengah makan. まず標準形を覚え、話し言葉は聞いて分かるようにしましょう。balik と pulang はどちらも「家に帰る」で、日常会話でよく聞くのは balik です。

Unit 4B · Culture and usage note|3|8.source_text: Kata-Kata のカードには語の注記もあります。minggu depan は来週、minggu lepas は先週です（カード ms-c04-019、ms-c04-020）。depan には「前」、lepas には「〜の後」という意味もあります。baru のカード（ms-c04-041）には、同じ語が「新しい」という意味にもなると書かれています。これは第6章で学びます。

Unit 4B · Teaching plan and answer key|3.source_text: Before Block A: Kata-Kata Sedia Kelas c04 (26 cards, frames ms-c04-f01 and ms-c04-f02).
Before Block E: Kata-Kata Dunia "Satu hari Encik Tanaka" and "Bangun pagi"; learners only need to recognise the scene words.

After Block D: the Kata-Kata chapter 4 deck with spaced review, frames ms-c04-f03, ms-c04-f04, ms-c04-f05, ms-c04-f06, ms-c04-f07 in the frame drill and Susun Ayat; about 3 hours of self-study for this unit (planning figure).
Hanashishou starts at A2, so there is no Hanashishou scene for this unit. Listening uses the teacher-read script.
■ Block A · Words and patterns (45 min)
Goal: I can describe my daily routine with times and say what I have done, am doing and will do.
0–5 Recall: unit 4A time, day and frequency (opener prompts).
5–10 Tanya Cikgu questions from Kata-Kata.
10–20 Vocabulary focus: core words first; Dunia and revision words are only pointed out.
20–40 Pattern focus: patterns 1 to 5 (sudah / belum, sedang / masih, akan, pernah, mula / habis), Q&A first, rule second.
40–45 First substitutions (Drill 2, items 1 to 3).
■ Block B · Drills and conversation (45 min)
Goal: I can ask and answer Sudah …? questions and use belum, masih and pernah.
0–5 Recall: Sudah makan? round the class; each learner answers Sudah or Belum.
5–25 Drill ladder in order: pattern table, substitution, time-cue transformation, question and answer, question-word choice, short dialogues, then the timeline drill.
25–40 Model conversation, gapped form, then the changed-facts variant.
40–45 Pair rehearsal without the script.
■ Block C · Listening and task (45 min)
Goal: I can follow a description of someone's day and reply to a message about a changed meeting.
0–5 Recall: learners say what they did this morning and what they will do tonight.
5–20 Listening: read the questions, two readings, check, then shadow three lines.
20–30 Reading and writing.
30–45 Task with role cards; announce the change of plan halfway.

Unit 4B · Teaching plan and answer key|4.source_text: Goal: I can check my use of the tense markers and daily verbs in a short test.
0–15 Mixed review: cumulative question-word drill (chapters 1 to 4), then the timeline drill with new cues.
35–45 Preview: chapter 5 Kata-Kata set (adjectives); the review block for chapters 1 to 4 comes next.
Goal: I can recognise words for a working day and a morning at home in two Kata-Kata Dunia scenes.
0–5 Recall: what time you got up and what you have not done yet today.
5–15 Kata-Kata Dunia scenes "Satu hari Encik Tanaka" and "Bangun pagi" as listening (teacher reads, learners point to pictures or words).
30–40 Free variation: the alarm clock does not ring, or the boss arrives early.
■ What to listen for · 注意点
Standard first: sudah before spoken dah; sedang before spoken tengah. Once both are on the board, accept spoken forms in pair work.

ke (to) is a chapter 7 word, so this unit uses pergi kerja, balik rumah and sampai di …, which are everyday Malaysian speech. Sam (12 Nov 2026): show ke in explainers and notes to sensitise learners, but do not drill or test it before chapter 7.
With semalam a plain verb is natural (Semalam saya balik lambat); sudah is not required. With esok or minggu depan, akan is optional.
If Sudah …? is answered Tidak where "not yet" is meant, model Belum.
Root verbs only (makan, minum, tidur, mandi, pergi, bangun, mula, datang); affixed forms wait for chapters 10 and 11.
Dunia words from "Satu hari Encik Tanaka" and "Bangun pagi" are for recognition in Block E only.

Unit 4B · Review block · Chapters 1 to 4.source_text: ■ Your turn · 自分で
Part 1 (10 min): without notes, ask your partner one question from each chapter: a greeting (1), a name or home (2), a price or an age (3), a time, a day or a Sudah …? question (4).
Part 2 (20 min): write four sentences about yesterday and tomorrow with semalam, sudah, esok and akan. Fictional details are fine.
Part 3 (15 min): read your partner's sentences aloud and ask two questions with bila or pukul berapa.
パート1：各章から一つずつ質問。パート2：昨日と明日について4文。パート3：相手の文を読み、bila・pukul berapa で質問。
■ Peer check · 互いに確認
☐ The greeting fits the time of day (chapter 1).
☐ Title before the name; no awak to a senior (chapter 2).
☐ Numbers and prices are correct (chapter 3).
☐ pukul for the clock, jam for how long; the marker fits the time word (chapter 4).
Model: Semalam saya bangun pukul enam. Saya pergi kerja pukul tujuh setengah. Esok saya akan main badminton pukul lapan pagi. Selepas itu, saya akan kemas rumah.
